messages.content: Translate CURRENT source rules into a compact Python program, returned in the code string. Use meaningful variables and ordinary arithmetic, comparisons, Boolean and/or/not, and conditional expressions. This program is parsed without executing arbitrary Python and passes the existing source, type, scope, resource and completion checks. No imports, tools, loops, attributes or extra output. A public numeric/string input is a plain assignment with exact evidence comment: variable = literal # sN. Do not enumerate or copy source paragraphs into variables. Derived quantities are expressions. Factual predicates remain unresolved: b_name = observation(EXACT_ENTITY, FACT_SOURCE_ID, EXACT_RULE_PREDICATE, RULE_SOURCE_ID). Quotes must be literal substrings of the indicated source. Do not supply their truth values. Never use an observation for a legal conclusion, numeric comparison, threshold, year or date calculation. A partly untranslated legal subexpression uses b_name = residual(RULE_SOURCE_ID, EXACT_PROPER_SUBQUOTE); the containing rule must read it. It stays both true/false, never a guessed answer. A legal output is a no-argument function: decorate with @rule("sN", "sM", otherwise=EXPLICIT_DISABLED_VALUE), then def meaningful_name(): return EXPRESSION. The sources are precisely the full rules actually translated. Its disabled value must be supplied explicitly with the correct type; it is not inferred. Applicability is a no-argument function with @scope("sN") and return BOOLEAN_EXPRESSION. Every inherited applicability scope is physically enforced on affected rule outputs by the source context. Literal True is allowed as scope only for structural titles; actual conditions require executable predicates. Unused scopes, ordinary calculations and references do not cover untranslated rules. Declare each name once; reference a rule result by its name or a no-argument call. Finish with query = EXPRESSION using guarded rule outputs and the exact native output shape. Do not substitute a native answer literal, an unguarded local result or a fallback. Python lists/dictionaries and min/max are supported. All branches must type check. Exact division uses an integer denominator; monetary results must remain exact. Partial source remains unresolved; do not invent missing rules to claim completion. Earlier examples teach syntax only; CURRENT has its own entities, years, rules and native result.
